transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-09-21
Start: 14:00 UTC
Duration: ~55 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Liam O'Neill (Redwood SE), Sofia Park (Redwood CSM), Jordan Lee (Cedar Procurement), Anita Singh (Cedar Legal), Rafael Ortiz (Cedar CTO), Priya Nair (Cedar Security), Ethan Brooks (Cedar Finance)
Shared artifacts: Redwood MSA (drive link), DPA draft (drive link), Pricing worksheet (sheet link), SOC2/ISO certs (redwood.link/soc2.pdf)

Auto-summary (auto-generated, may be imperfect):
- Review of MSA redlines, DPA clauses for data residency and deletion, SLA targets and credits, pricing approval path and pilot/onboarding timeline.
- Action: Redwood to send redlined MSA + pricing scenarios; Cedar legal to review liability cap/indemnity language; security to validate KMS/HSM and audit log requirements.

Transcript:
[00:00] Maya Chen: All right, everyone, thanks for joining on time, appreciate it. I think we've got about 55 minutes, we'll run through the MSA redlines, DPA points, SLA ask, and pricing approvals. Liam will jump in on the technical side.
[00:12] Jordan Lee: Thanks Maya. From procurement's side we just want to lock timeline and any must-haves for legal and security so we can clear budget committee end of next week.
[00:20] Anita Singh: Hi, yes, hi. I'll be focusing on liability, data processing obligations, sub-processing, and termination rights.
[00:29] Liam O'Neill: Hi all. I'll cover the VPC options and private deployment checklist. Quick note: some names in the docs may be older, I think the DPA says KV cache which it meant to say K-V cache, small transcription typo but ok.
[00:43] Rafael Ortiz: Rafael here. Quick question - we have a strict data residency requirement in EU for certain PII. Can you confirm you have region pinning and on-prem options?
[00:52] Maya Chen: Yes, we have region pinning for hosted, and our Private deployment supports VPC/on-prem with customer-managed networking. We'll put the deployment options in the summary.
[01:10] Priya Nair: From security: we require bring-your-own-key with HSM-backed KMS and audit logs for every request. Is BYOK available?
[01:18] Liam O'Neill: Yes, BYOK is supported for Private, and for Dedicated we have KMS integration; HSM is supported via customer KMS. We will send the KMS integration doc.
[01:32] Jordan Lee: Great. On the MSA - on page 6, the limitation of liability is currently standard. Our legal would like to propose a higher cap for breaches that involve customer PII, is that something you can negotiate?
[01:44] Maya Chen: I can take that back - typically we have a liability cap tied to fees or a fixed number, but for regulated customers we can discuss. I'll flag that with our legal.
[01:55] Anita Singh: Also we need to confirm subcontractor list and subprocessors in the DPA, and a flow for notifications when a subprocessor is added. Can you confirm?
[02:05] Maya Chen: We maintain a subprocessors list in the console and push notifications for material changes. We'll share the current list and the notification cadence.
[02:18] Ethan Brooks: On pricing - our CFO wants to see committed vs on-demand scenarios. We need a pricing worksheet showing 12-month commit, 3-month pilot, and an elastic option.
[02:28] Sofia Park: We have a pricing sheet template we'll send, with committed discounts and burst options. We'll include sample TCO.
[02:36] Jordan Lee: Ok, procurement needs pricing approved by Friday to hit the finance approver.
[02:42] Maya Chen: Understood. We'll prioritize the committed scenarios and send the sheet by tomorrow EOD.

[02:55] [15:00] (transcription jump - auto segment)
[15:01] Anita Singh: On indemnification, we have some standard language around IP claims; we want to ensure it's mutual where possible, and carveouts for open-source.
[15:12] Maya Chen: Right, mutual indemnity is something we evaluate. For open-source there's usually a carve-out. I'll note that for legal.
[15:25] Rafael Ortiz: Technical Q - can Redwood support private deployments behind our firewall for the pilot? We want to run sensitive queries in a VPC and use a Redwood-managed control plane but customer data plane.
[15:40] Liam O'Neill: We support a split control/data plane for Private customers. For pilot we can do a dedicated pool in your VPC or a light on-prem package. We have a network diagram, will send. Note: some features like streaming may require specific egress configs.
[15:58] Priya Nair: About logging - we need immutable audit logs and retention to 7 years for certain records. Does Redwood support custom retention policies?
[16:10] Liam O'Neill: Audit logs are configurable in Private; retention windows can be set and logs can be exported to your S3/GCS bucket. For hosted we have 90/365 day options currently. We'll include an export strategy.
[16:26] Jordan Lee: On SLAs - we are asking for 99.9% uptime and token latency p50/p95 targets. Can you outline what's possible for hosted vs dedicated vs private?
[16:38] Maya Chen: Our Dedicated SLA can support 99.9% with a latency SLO that depends on model and instance types. Hosted tier has a best-effort SLA with credits for system-wide outages; dedicated comes with 99.9% uptime SLA and an ops playbook. For private deployments we can negotiate SLAs as part of enterprise contract. We'll provide an SLA matrix.
[16:58] Anita Singh: And credits - do you offer service credits tied to latency breaches or only downtime?
[17:06] Maya Chen: We offer credits for both downtime and for missing SLOs in Dedicated/Enterprise agreements; the DPA will include the specifics.
[17:15] Anita Singh: We need clear definitions (downtime, incident classification, MTTR, reporting).
[17:21] Liam O'Neill: Yep, the SLA doc includes incident severity definitions and MTTR targets.
[17:30] [23:45] Speaker 1: Sorry small audio glitch.
[23:50] Rafael Ortiz: For onboarding timeline - how long from signature to pilot? We're aiming for 4 weeks.
[23:58] Sofia Park: Typical timeline: signature + 1 week kickoff, 2 weeks provisioning and network ops, 1 week pilot and smoke tests - so 4 weeks is doable if procurement and security review proceed on schedule.
[24:15] Jordan Lee: Good. Procurement will need an onboarding checklist for internal stakeholders - security, infra, legal, and product.
[24:22] Maya Chen: We'll provide a checklist and an internal RACI.
[24:30] Priya Nair: A couple security details - encryption at rest+in transit mandatory, KMS BYOK, key rotation policies, and quarterly pen tests. Also question about telemetry - do you redact PII from logs?
[24:45] Liam O'Neill: We can configure PII redaction at ingestion, and for Private deployments logs can be fully customer-controlled. For hosted, we have options to mask or not retain input content based on retention settings and DPA.
[24:58] Anita Singh: The DPA clause on deletion seems okay but we want a 30-day guaranteed purge on termination for our EU data. Can you confirm?
[25:07] Maya Chen: We can commit to 30-day purge for EU-hosted customer data in Private or Dedicated; for hosted standard we have 60 days in the standard DPA but we can propose 30 days for regulated customers - we'll include in redline.
[25:22] Ethan Brooks: Regarding pricing approvals - are there published enterprise price bands or is it custom?
[25:30] Maya Chen: We have published bands for self-serve, and a commercial pricing band for committed enterprise business. We'll share the committed discount table.
[25:40] Jordan Lee: Another procurement ask - do you support standard ediscovery and audit cooperation clauses for legal holds?
[25:47] Maya Chen: Yes, we have an addendum for legal hold and eDiscovery support; we'll include that.
[25:55] Anita Singh: On insurance, will you be able to provide a certificate of insurance with cyber liability limits?
[26:02] Maya Chen: Yes, we can provide COIs and evidence of cyber insurance.
[26:10] Rafael Ortiz: Performance benchmarking - we'll want Redwood to run a short benchmark for our typical prompt patterns and token counts. Can you do that as part of pilot?
[26:20] Liam O'Neill: Absolutely, we'll run a benchmark using your prompt set, measure p50/p95 latency and cost per 1k tokens, and share the result. We'll need a sample dataset and expected concurrency.
[26:32] Jordan Lee: How do approvals flow? Once pricing and legal are aligned, is there an e-sign process?
[26:39] Maya Chen: We use DocuSign for MSA; DPA can be attached. We'll send DocuSign links and a summary of redlines.
[26:48] [31:00] (brief pause)
[31:05] Priya Nair: A question about multi-tenant hosted: are there tenant isolation guarantees, and do you run tenant-level encryption keys?
[31:15] Liam O'Neill: For hosted multi-tenant we logically isolate and encrypt keys at rest but BYOK is only available on Dedicated/Private. Tenant isolation is standard but we can move to Dedicated for stronger isolation.
[31:28] Anita Singh: Regarding export controls and data transfers, we need to confirm standard SCCs or alternative transfer mechanisms for EU data.
[31:36] Maya Chen: We'll include our transfer mechanism details and SCCs; if needed, we can add an addendum.
[31:45] Jordan Lee: One more - termination assistance. We need a clause that outlines export of customer data in machine-readable form within 30 days and assistance for transition.
[31:54] Maya Chen: That is standard; we'll include timeline and format.
[32:05] [40:00] Speaker 2: small crosstalk
[40:06] Sofia Park: I'll put together an onboarding timeline doc with kickoff agenda, roles, testing plan and cutover steps. I'll aim to send by Monday.
[40:15] Maya Chen: I'll own the MSA redlines and coordinate with legal; Liam will send the KMS and network diagrams and run through the pilot benchmark plan.
[40:25] Anita Singh: We'll review redlines and get back by next Thursday. Rafael will validate network diagrams with infra.
[40:33] Rafael Ortiz: Yes, I'll review and make sure our cloud team is comfortable.
[40:40] Ethan Brooks: Finance will need final pricing and payment terms in writing to release funds.
[40:46] Maya Chen: We'll include payment schedule options in the pricing worksheet.
[40:52] Jordan Lee: Good. Any outstanding blockers?
[41:00] Priya Nair: Security sign-off is the main gate but seems addressable.
[41:05] Anita Singh: Liability cap negotiation is the main legal item.
[41:10] Maya Chen: Noted. We'll aim to surface proposed wording in the redline.
[41:18] [51:30] Closing
[51:35] Maya Chen: Thanks everyone - recap of next steps: Maya send redlined MSA by Friday 9/24, Liam send KMS & network docs 9/25, Sofia send onboarding timeline 9/27, Redwood to deliver pricing scenarios by tomorrow EOD. Cedar legal to review and respond by 9/30. We'll schedule the technical onboarding call for 9/28 - I'll Doodle for times.
[51:58] Jordan Lee: Thanks, appreciate it.
[52:02] Anita Singh: Thanks all.
[52:05] Rafael Ortiz: Bye.

End of transcript.
